FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 28) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the 
Fragrance and Flavour Ingredients Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related 
Products Division Council. 


Proper storage of essential oil is very important to protect it from heat, light and moisture etc. Essential oils should 
be stored in proper containers which do not cause any change in the composition of the oil even after long storage 
periods. Bulk containers or small scale containers are used for the shipment and storage of essential oils. They 
should be fabricated from inert materials such as galvanized, tinned or enamelled iron, aluminum, stainless steel or 
glass with appropriate closures. 


In the formulation of this Indian Standard, considerable assistance has been taken from ISO/TR 210 : 1999 ‘Essential 
oils — General rules forpackaging, conditioning and storage’. This standard does not provide general rules for 
use of essential oils in pharmaceuticals and foods. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised)’. 


IS 326 (Part 28) : 2017 


Indian Standard 


METHODS OF SAMPLING AND TEST FOR NATURAL 
AND SYNTHETIC PERFUMERY MATERIAL 


PART 28 GENERAL RULES FOR PACKAGING, CONDITIONING AND STORAGE 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard describes the materials to be used 
for the containers intended for containing essential oils, 
depending on the end use. 


1.2 It also gives general rules and recommendations 
relating to the properties of these containers, their 
conditioning and storage. 

NOTE — Essential oils are used for different purposes, for 


example, perfumery and cosmetic use; reference samples or test 
samples; industrial raw materials etc. 


2 COMPOSITION OF THE CONTAINERS 


2.1 General 


2.1.1 Essential oils shall be packed in containers 
which, by their nature, do not cause alteration of the 
product and which protect it against any external 
attack. 


2.1.2 The container materials shall be inert towards 
the packed product so as to prevent any 
simultaneous damage of the product and of the 
material. 


2.2 Materials for Containers Intended for 
Containing Essential Oils for Perfumery and 
Cosmetic Use 


All the materials listed under 2.2 may be used, on 
condition that they do not alter the composition of the 
essential oil or its characteristic properties, for example, 
appearance, color, odour, etc. 


2.2.1 Glass 


Glass containers of such type may be used which 
maintain the characteristic properties of essential oil as 
unchanged. 


NOTE — Type III glass (soda-calcic glass) is advisable as it 
maintains unchanged characteristic properties of the essential 
oils. Tinted anti-actinic glass is always recommended. 


2.2.2 Metals and Alloys 
2.2.2.1 Stainless steel 


These materials shall contain at least 13 percent of 
chromium.Theymay also contain nickel and/or 
manganese. 


Furthermore, one or more of the following elements 


may be included, provided they do not exceed the limit 
given in Table 1 for each of them. 


Table 1 
(Clause 2.2.2.1)

q) (2) (3) 
i) Tantalum 1 
ii) Niobium 1 
iiii) Zirconium 1 
iv) Molybdenum 4 
v) Titanium 4 
vi) Aluminium 4 
viii) Copper 4 


2.2.2.2 Aluminium and aluminum alloys 


Aluminium shall be at least 99 percent pure.The total 
content of impurities shall not exceed 1 percent, and 
they are limited as given in Table 2.

The anodic layer may be coloured by pigments or 
colourings. 


A compulsory final filling operation is carried out with 
the exception of the aluminium or aluminium alloy 
materials and products anodized in a phosphoric 
medium or covered by coating. This operation shall be 
carried out with distilled or demineralized water 
containing either 8 g/l of nickel acetate and 1 g/l of 
cobalt acetate or one ofthese two salts at the maximum 
concentration indicated. 


All the technical conditions, particularly, the 
temperature and the standing time shall be chosen in 
such a way that, at the end of the operation, the oxide 
layer formed during the anodization process loses its 
absorption power due to its natural porosity, and 
acquires optimum inertness. 


2.2.2.3 Tin 


The material shall contain at least 97 percent of tin, 
determined as metastannic acid, and not more than 0.5 
percent of lead or 300 mg/kg of arsenic. 


2.2.2.4 Copper, zinc and galvanized iron 


Copper and iron are not advisable as they are oxidation 


catalysts. Except during the distillation process, direct 
contact between the essential oil and these materials is 
forbidden. 


2.2.3 Polymers: Plastics and Varnishes 


Plastics materials intended for containing essential oils 
for perfumery and cosmetic use shall be submitted to 
prior testing, concerning 


a) an identification; 

b) their permeability to carbon dioxide, oxygen, 
steam, fragrances, etc., and 

c) the ageing ofthe packed product; 

d) a determination of certain substances such as 
antioxidant monomer residues, anti-U Vs, 
stabilizers, catalyst residues, heavy metals or 
aromatic diamines. 


Only those substances listed in the national regulations, 
which also include migration limits for some of these 
substances are authorized as components of plastics 
materials. 


2.2.4 Ceramic, Vitrified or Enamelled Materials Used 
for Internal Coatings 


These materials shall not release lead and cadmium in 
larger quantities than those laid down by the national 
regulations. 


2.3 Materials for Containers Intended for Containing 
Reference Samples or Test Samples of Essential Oils 


The only recommended material is tinted anti-actinic 
glass. 


2.4 Materials for Containers Intended for Containing 
Essential Oils used as Industrial Raw Materials 


Tinted anti-actinic glass is recommended, but all the 
materials in 2.2 may also be used. 


3 PIGMENTS OR COLOURING 


3.1 They shall have a high level of purity and the 
maximum content in mineral elements is given in 
Table 4. 


Table 4 
(Clause 3.1)

i) (2) (3) 
i) Antimony 0.05 
ii) Arsenic 0.01 
iii) Barium 0.01 
iv) Cadmium 0.01 
v) Chromium 0.1 
vi) Lead 0.01 
vii) Mercury 0.005 
viii) Selenium 0.01 


4 CHARACTERISTICS OF CONTAINERS 
INTENDED FOR CONTAININGESSENTIAL OILS 


4.1 Types 


The containers intended for containing essential oils 
differ in shape, nature and capacity.They shall be 
appropriate for their use (following the 
recommendations relating to the materials given 
in 2).The most frequently used types of container are 
the following: 


a) flasks; 
b) cans; 
c) barrels; 
d) drums; 
e) tanks. 


Drums of capacity equal to or greater than 200 1 shall 
be provided with hoops or with moulded ribs. 


4.2 Capacity 


The capacity of the containers used differs according 
to the projected use.It varies from a few millilitres to 
several thousand litres. 


4.3 Closures 


4.3.1 The closure materials, including the joints screw- 
type corks, shall be inert to the essential oils and shall 
be submitted to compatibility tests. 


4.3.2 The materials which may be used are glass, tin 
plate, stainless steel, compatible and inert plastics, etc. 


4.3.3 Cork which has not been treated previously is 
not advisable due to its porosity and because it contains 
waxes and tannins which are liable to be dissolved in 
the essential oils. 


4.3.4 Pre-treated cork may be used if its chemical 
inertness towards the essential oil placed in contact with 
it can be proven. 


4.3.5 The closures or caps shall be as tight as possible. 
After closing, the containers shall be protected by a 
seal guaranteeing inviolability. 


4.4 External Solderings 


Whatever the container and the destination of the 
essential oil inside, the use of tin and lead alloy is 
authorized for external solderings, but it is 
recommended to use other soldering processes such as 
electric soldering. 


IS 326 (Part 28) : 2017 


5 CONDITIONING AND STORAGE 


5.1 Conditioning 


5.1.1 Containers intended to contain essential oils shall 
be new or in good condition, clean and dry (dried by 
dry steam) and perfectly tight. 


5.1.2 Ifthey have already served for other uses, it shall 
be ensured that they do not contain any products likely 
to alter the quality of the essential oil. 


5.1.3 Glass containers which are not made of tinted 
anti-actinic glass shall be protected from light. 


5.1.4 The containers shall not be completely filled. A 
head space, the volume of which is determined following 
the expected changes in temperature conditions during 
transport (in general, this represents a maximum of 
5 percent to 10 percent depending on the capacity of 
the container), shall be left free. 


5.1.5 This head space between the essential oil and the 
container shall be filled with nitrogen or another inert 
gas at the time of filling. 


5.2 Storage 


5.2.1 Essential oils are flammable liquids and shall be 
stored in special places. 


5.2.2 It is necessary, in addition, to check that the 
containers do not permit any loss of liquid or vapour. 


5.2.3 The containers shall be protected against any 
accidental breakage. 


5.2.4 They shall be stored in a place sheltered from 
light and maintained at a temperature. 


5.3 Special Cases 


5.3.1 By agreement between the parties concerned, it 
may be that, only for transportation, the essential oils 
are provisionally packed in containers made of 
aluminium or tin-plate.In this case, the essential oils 
shall be decanted on receipt into tinted anti-actinic glass 
containers for storage. 


5.3.2 Any container which has been opened, either for 
decantation or the taking of samples, shall be re- 
stoppered immediately after use in such a way it will be 
as tight as possible. 


5.3.3 Ifthere is a large quantity of the essential oil taken 
from the container, the remaining essential oil shall be 
decanted into a smaller container for storage.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
